name: DPP exchange profile epcis-event-vc@1: EPCIS events as VC 2.0 credentials keyed by their Event Hash ID, signed ES256K as compact JWS by the party's published credential key, with their findings and anchor fields
notes: checkedAt is fixed so the time findings are reproducible. Two parties sign: their identity key scalars are published in keys, the credential key of each is the BRC-42 child under [1, "dpp epcis event v1"] with key identifier "credential" and counterparty anyone, and each issuer is the did:key of that credential key. Nothing derived from these scalars will ever hold value. The JWS bytes are the committed representation: digest_hex is SHA-256 over the exact string.

vectors.description: The commissioning event signed by party A under its one published credential key, the BRC-42 child of its identity key under [1, "dpp epcis event v1"] and the key identifier "credential", published as a did:key. The hash ID is the credential id, the signature verifies against the kid, the interval includes checkedAt, no status entry, no authority policy.

The same credential serialised with another member order and whitespace, signed by the same party: a different byte string with a different digest and the same id. Its proof holds. A registry that already holds a credential for this hash ID and issuer refuses it: one party signs one event once, unless the bytes are equal.

expected.pair_rule: refused: a second byte string for a hash ID and issuer the registry already holds

vectors.description: The same event signed by party B: a second attestation of one hash ID by another issuer, accepted beside the first.

expected.pair_rule: accepted: a different issuer for the same hash ID

vectors.description: The positive credential with the subject's recordTime changed after signing: the hash ID still holds, because recordTime is not hashed, and the signature fails.
The positive credential with the subject's bizStep changed after signing: the subject no longer hashes to the id (and the signature fails); the proof reports the hash mismatch first.
The positive credential re-headed with party B's kid: a kid that names no verification method of the issuer fails the proof before any key is tried.
A subject whose eventID is a hash ID other than the one it hashes to: the credential id is right and the subject contradicts it.
A subject carrying an errorDeclaration cannot be hashed under @1 and the proof fails by that name.
A subject naming an EPC scheme outside the @1 subset: the hash is uncomputable and the proof fails by that name.
The transaction event names one EPC, a source party and a destination party; the subjects are the object identifiers only, sorted, and the anchor subject is the first.
The sensor observation under an inline prefix declaration carried as the third context entry.
A credential with a Bitstring Status List entry verified without a status verifier: status is unknown, never passed.
The positive credential re-headed as ES256: another suite, reported unsupported, not failed.
Two parts are not a compact JWS.
A member the profile does not define (name) is a shape failure.
A did:web issuer whose kid resolves through the caller's resolver to party A's credential key: the proof holds; without a resolver it is unknown.
